A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, From Noise to Narrative. Their text, equations, figures, tables, appendices, and checklists support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SAE training, input-perturbation experiments, hallucination prediction on 1,006 summaries, and interventions suppressing hallucination-associated concepts.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds image-error prediction and comparative hallucination-detection results on question-answering benchmarks.

M1.justification: The core SAE training, PLS prediction, and VIP-based suppression procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D adds an auxiliary linear classifier using only layer-6 L0 counts to predict CLIP misclassification, a limited additional prediction procedure.

E1.justification: v2 expands evaluation beyond the retained image/text perturbation and summarization tasks to TruthfulQA generation and multiple choice, TriviaQA generation, and CoQA generation. Appendix D also adds prediction of image-classification errors on natural and patch-shuffled ImageNet images.

E2.justification: Unlike v1, v2 directly evaluates established hallucination detectors against PLS concepts. Tables 9–11 include Perplexity, Energy Score, Lexical Similarity, Normalized Entropy, and EigenScore; Table 12 includes only Perplexity and Energy Score as external comparators.

E3.justification: The added QA experiments use AUC, benchmark-specific labels derived from answer metrics, and shared cross-validation folds through Language Model Evaluation Harness. The new vision protocol uses 9,000 images and separately evaluates natural and 56x56-patch-shuffled inputs. Existing experimental settings are retained; the newly stated 32-image steerability criterion is additional documentation.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds a focused analysis comparing L0-only and PLS-concept predictors of image errors, including their behavior under patch shuffling. Existing perturbation-severity analyses, initialization-overlap tests, concept examples, and suppression experiments remain unchanged.

E5.justification: v1 already reports ten-fold cross-validation and standard deviations. The new tables follow the same mean-plus-standard-deviation practice across ten folds; no new uncertainty-estimation procedure or formal significance test is reported.

E6.justification: Tables 8–12 add substantial results. For example, TriviaQA AUC is 70.8 ± 2.6 for layer-11 PLS versus 68.9 ± 2.9 for Lexical Similarity, whereas CoQA exact-match detection favors Lexical Similarity, 66.4 ± 1.6 versus 53.9 ± 2.6. Section 5 also corrects the best summarization layer from 13 to 11, retaining R2 = 0.271 ± 0.010 and the unchanged Figure 5.

T1.justification: No theoretical results or proofs are introduced. The explicit decoder equation and simplified reconstruction-loss notation in Section 2.2 restate the existing mathematics; the PLS and VIP formulas are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and three numbered contributions retain the same central claims: semantic structure emerges from noise, concept activation expands with input disorder, and input-derived concepts predict output hallucination. Added benchmark evidence supports the existing prediction claim without redefining these contributions.

C2.justification: The limitations discussion newly identifies sequence length and sampling temperature as untested factors and predicts increased hallucination and concept activation. Appendix E acknowledges the CoQA exception to comparative success, while Appendix D distinguishes increased image-error frequency from ease of predicting individual errors.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies that steerability requires label changes in all 32 sampled neutral images and identifies the evaluation harness for added benchmarks. Appendix G supplies an explicit code repository location, whereas v1 only refers to supplementary scripts. Existing hyperparameter, hardware, and training-time information is retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references supporting the new detectors, TriviaQA, CoQA, BLEU, and ROUGE, and contrasts input-only prediction with detectors requiring generated output. Section 6's broader research positioning remains unchanged; reference reordering and duplicate consolidation do not remove prior research coverage.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify SAE reconstruction, per-layer training, and concept evaluation, improve cross-references, and update author and conference information. Appendix G is added and references are alphabetized, but the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds a substantial comparative display suite in Tables 8–12, covering vision prediction and several QA evaluation settings. All 16 existing figures are retained, and the previous qualitative Table 8 becomes Table 13. Front matter and figure placement also undergo layout changes.

improvement.justification: The new baseline comparisons make the practical detection claim more assessable and reveal its CoQA limitation. Correcting the best-layer attribution and clarifying reproducibility also improve the paper. However, the new benchmark descriptions leave binary-label construction underspecified, and no significance test accompanies the claim of significant superiority, limiting the strength of the added evidence.
